\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F30E SUGAR EXPORTS TO THE US JUMP 512% — SHEINBAUM’S “EXTRAORDINARY NEWS”

While Washington rattles the tariff saber, the USDA just announced it will import 1.15 million tons of Mexican sugar next cycle — a 512% jump that channels up to 4,760 million pesos to 170,000 cane farmers, benefiting as many as 500,000 families. Talks began in November when the US Agriculture Secretary came to Sheinbaum. She called it “noticia extraordinaria.”

🇲🇽🏭 TRUMP GLOATED ABOUT TOYOTA — HE LEFT OUT THE PART WHERE MEXICO KEEPS THE PLANT

Toyota will shift one truck line — the Tacoma — from Tijuana to Texas by 2030 under Washington's 25% auto tariff, and Trump crowed "tariffs in action." What he skipped: Toyota keeps its Guanajuato plant and 2,800 direct jobs, while Sheinbaum says another automaker will invest 500 million dollars in Mexico to fill the gap. Tariff theater meets the reality of a market you can't relocate.

Source: La Jornada / El Financiero

🔥🇲🇽 39 CASINO GROUPS UNDER THE MICROSCOPE — MEXICO TRACKS CARTEL MONEY LAUNDERING

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF), coordinating with the US Treasury's OFAC, is monitoring 39 authorized gambling operators for laundering drug money — and has already sanctioned seven casinos tied to the Sinaloa and Northeast cartels. Investigators documented "unusual transactions of up to 50 million pesos" funneled to fintechs in the US and Europe, and imposed 6 billion pesos in fines in 2025 alone. The schemes hook students and retirees through identity theft.

Source: Contralínea

⚖️🇲🇽 MEXICO'S JUDICIAL REFORM GOES DIGITAL — 5,000 AUTHORITIES ORDERED ONLINE, 180 DAYS TO COMPLY

The Órgano de Administración Judicial has ordered every federal, state and municipal authority — all three branches of the State — to interconnect with the judiciary's electronic amparo system within an unextendable 180 days. Mandated by the reformed Ley de Amparo, officials say full digitization will cut judicial timelines roughly in half. The paper-shuffling that let the powerful stall amparos for years is being switched off.

Source: La Jornada

🌊🇲🇽 MEXICO IS BRINGING LAKE PÁTZCUARO BACK — 42 SPRINGS REHABILITATED, MILLIONS OF TREES IN THE GROUND

Where neoliberal governments left Michoacán's Purépecha lake to die, the 4T's Temporary Employment Program has rehabilitated 42 of 79 springs this year and is planting 2.5 million trees in the basin — on top of 3.5 million already sown. The lake has recovered roughly 500 hectares of water in two years. Ecological restoration run as paid public work, not privatization.

Source: La Jornada

🇲🇽🎨 "Public education is the best education there is." Defending universal scholarships against critics who would tie aid to grades, President Sheinbaum said Mexico's public schools are the best precisely because of their teachers. In Zacatecas, 180,627 students receive Welfare Scholarships backed by more than 1.6 billion pesos — 83,353 primary students newly added. Nationwide, Education Secretary Mario Delgado reported 22 million recipients this year and the "Vive Saludable, Vive Feliz" health program reaching 10.8 million children. — Claudia Sheinbaum, Becas para el Bienestar, Zacatecas · July 12, 2026

🇲🇽✊ Scholarships from primary school to university — for every public-school student. "If you were born in Zacatecas and study in Zacatecas, from primary school to university, if you study in a public school: scholarships, scholarships, scholarships and more scholarships." — Claudia Sheinbaum, Becas para el Bienestar, Zacatecas · July 12, 2026 The Rita Cetina scholarship pays 2,500 pesos every August for school supplies and uniforms — now covering every public primary student. Nationwide, Becas para el Bienestar reach 12.8 million students backed by a 23.6-billion-peso investment.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO EXITS THE SLUMP: LEADING INDICATOR HITS HIGHEST SINCE 2022

INEGI’s leading indicator rose to 100.9 units in May — its 14th straight monthly gain and highest reading since 2022 — while the coincident indicator posted a 7th consecutive rise. The data confirms Mexico shook off the weakness of late 2025 and early 2026, with analysts projecting a second-quarter GDP rebound driven by construction, consumption and tourism.

🚨🇲🇽 SIX OF 17 MEXICANS KILLED IN ICE CUSTODY DIED OF MEDICAL NEGLECT

Of the 17 Mexican nationals who have died in ICE custody under Trump this year, six died from medical complications and negligence, four from alleged suicides, and three from force used during arrests — and 14 of the 17 died inside detention centers run by private companies. Mexico is escalating from diplomatic notes to the criminal courts: the SRE will file cease-and-desist letters against the firms operating those centers, President Sheinbaum confirmed.

REUTERS: Mexico Expects Economy to Outperform IMF Projections
July 8, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Straight reporting, no editorializing: Reuters runs Finance Minister Edgar Amador's line that Mexico will beat the IMF's downgraded 1.2% growth forecast for 2026.

🇲🇽 Amador ties the IMF's cut to "the shock to the energy market caused by tensions in the Persian Gulf" — a global revision, not a Mexican policy failure. Worth noting when the coverage is actually fair.

• "a global downward revision to the IMF's estimates for world economies"
